description: The quote inside an internal page's dark band, pulled up so it begins over the dragon curve. Marks quote and quoteAttribution against their frontmatter keys.
name: BandQuote

description: The ink band closing an internal page — dragon curve, heading and body copy, with the pulled-up quote opposite. Marks heading and bandBody; the Without Quote scenario shows the band as Contact renders it.
name: ExploratoryBand

description: The harmonograph standing in the left lane of a one-section internal page. Varies on two axes like the branching tree — per page at build time from a hashed seedKey, per visit in the browser — with the shared tree=static flag freezing both so captures stay deterministic. Unlike the tree it frames with meet rather than none, because the figure's whole subject is the ratio between two frequencies and an anisotropic stretch would silently rewrite that ratio on the way to the screen; the alignment is YMax so any residual letterboxing is taken off the top and the figure stays flush with the seam below.
name: Harmonograph

description: The home masthead — compass-rose mark, wordmark and kicker, centred. Carries the staged-preview field markers for the home entry's title and kicker; the kicker stays conditional, so a field the page does not render is one the preview leaves alone.
name: Masthead

description: An internal page's two-column header — mark and title left, standfirst opposite. Marks kicker, title and intro; the Title Only scenario shows the optional fields and their markers dropping together.
name: PageHeader

description: The prose block of an internal page, in either of two shapes chosen by the route from the body's own section count. The default 'columns' shape is two columns with the branching structure standing in the gap; 'single' is one centred column with a harmonograph in a lane to its left and a Voronoi field to its right, for a page that only says one thing and would otherwise leave a half-empty second column with the tree stranded beside it. Both shapes are held here behind a layout prop rather than split into two components, because the CMS body marker has to sit on the inner prose element in both and the foot slot's gutter bleed is shared; splitting would duplicate both and give the CMS two patch targets for one body field. The body marker sits on the inner prose element rather than the grid, because patching sets innerHTML and marking the grid would delete the structure SVGs on every staged body edit. Structures are bottom-anchored to the prose grid, so anything a page wants between its prose and the section below must go in the named foot slot rather than after the component: rendered as a sibling it pushes that section down while leaving the anchors behind, and the figures end in mid-air by exactly the sibling's height. In the single shape the lanes are grid items spanning both rows with the rows declared explicitly, since grid-row 1 / -1 resolves against the explicit grid and would otherwise collapse to the first row. Known limit: staged CMS preview patches the prose innerHTML in place, so editing a body from two sections down to one does not re-pick the layout until the next build — the layout is a build-time fact.
name: ProseColumns

description: The home ink band — night-variant mark, pull quote and attribution over a Koch fragment. The attribution marker carries the frontmatter key quoteAttribution rather than the component's attribution prop name.
name: QuoteBand

description: The site footer in its home and internal variants, which differ by gutter, foot depth and row alignment because the two designs genuinely differ — encoding both here keeps a fix to one page from restyling the other. The footer line is marked as setting text. The Contact link carries NO cms marker: its href is now a page url resolved from the nav singleton by resolveContactUrl, not a mailto built from settings.contactEmail, so the old href-only setting marker would let a staged contact-address edit patch a raw email address back over /contact.
name: SiteFooter

description: The internal-page navigation bar. Each menu item is marked on its li keyed by url, so a staged reorder matches by link rather than position and a removal takes the whole row; the site-title marker sits on the span so patching its text cannot delete the mark beside it. The current page is inked and teal-underlined and carries aria-current='page', so the highlight is announced as well as drawn; which item is current is decided by isCurrentNavPath rather than a string compare, because the stored nav url and the rendered pathname disagree about trailing slashes.
name: SiteNav

description: The home statement — heading, rendered markdown body and the closing lead line. Marks heading and lead as frontmatter fields and the body wrapper as the entry's markdown body, so a staged home edit patches each in place.
name: StatementBlock

description: The Voronoi field standing in the right lane of a one-section internal page, following the same two-axis pattern as the branching tree. The partition is computed across a rectangle a quarter larger than the lane while the viewBox is the lane itself, so the straight edges where clipping happened fall outside what is drawn and cells run off the top and bottom unresolved. preserveAspectRatio is none here and correct, because the field is generated at the lane's own 123x365 and there is no distortion to accept.
name: VoronoiField

description: Rewrites an on-page SVG to draw a freshly generated figure, reusing existing path elements, cloning the first as a template for extras and removing the surplus, so the styling stays defined only in the component's markup. The general form of what applyTreeGrowth did alone; three structures now regrow per visit and the Voronoi field genuinely changes path count between draws.
name: applyFigure

description: Writes a grown tree into an SVG already on the page, reframing the viewBox to match. Lives outside the Astro script tag so it is reachable from vitest: the new tree rarely has the same segment count as the one the server drew, so every call reuses, clones or removes path elements. Surplus paths are cloned from the server's own path, keeping stroke styling defined in exactly one place.
name: applyTreeGrowth

description: Displacement of one harmonograph axis at time t — two damped sinusoids summed, which is what the four-pendulum machine does mechanically. The unit of physics the whole figure is built from.
name: axisAt

description: Assembles a mailto: URL from a recipient and optional subject and body, percent-encoding each part.
name: buildMailto

untestabilityReason.justification: assembles a URL string from its arguments with no branching beyond omitting absent optional parts

description: One site's Voronoi cell: the frame cut back by the perpendicular bisector against every other site. The bisector is where the two squared distances are equal, and that difference is LINEAR in the point because the quadratic terms cancel — which is why successive half-plane clips are enough and no curve fitting is involved.
name: cellFor

description: A Voronoi cell's outline. A closed cell is a polygon; the open one is the same corners rotated so the missing edge is the closing one, then left unclosed, following openRectPath's three-sided square at the scale of a territory. Rotating rather than splicing keeps every drawn edge intact and removes exactly one.
name: cellPath

description: Clips a convex polygon to the half-plane where a linear edge function is negative, cutting new corners where the boundary crosses the line (Sutherland-Hodgman). The single geometric primitive the whole Voronoi partition is built from.
name: clipHalfPlane

description: Returns the spreadable data-cms-body attribute marking the element that renders an entry's rendered markdown body. Valueless in the CMS contract, so it emits the empty string, which Astro renders as a bare attribute that the presence selector still matches.
name: cmsBody

description: Returns the spreadable data-cms-entry attribute marking the element that renders one CMS entry, valued <collection>/<slug>. Returns an empty object for a missing or empty key, so pages that render no single entry emit no attribute at all rather than an empty one that would still match the patcher's [data-cms-entry] selector.
name: cmsEntry

description: Returns the spreadable data-cms-field attribute marking an element that renders one frontmatter field. The value is the FRONTMATTER key the CMS looks up, not the component's prop name — the two differ where a prop called attribution renders the quoteAttribution field.
name: cmsField

description: Returns the spreadable data-cms-nav-item attribute marking one menu entry, keyed by the url it points at so reordering the menu does not break the match. A NavItem whose url is absent — an item that only groups children — gets no attribute, since the url is the match key and a stringified undefined would read as a marker while matching nothing.
name: cmsNavItem

description: Returns the spreadable data-cms-setting attribute marking an element whose visible TEXT is one settings.json value. The CMS patcher sets textContent on the marked element, so it belongs on the element holding only that text.
name: cmsSetting

description: Returns the spreadable data-cms-setting-href attribute marking a link whose HREF is derived from a setting while its visible label stays fixed. Kept separate from cmsSetting because collapsing the two would let a staged contact-email edit overwrite the visible Contact label with a URL.
name: cmsSettingHref

description: Composes a page's head title as "Page · Site", returning the bare site title when the page passes no title or when its title already IS the site title — compared trimmed and case-insensitively, since both strings are CMS-editable. Feeds <title>, og:title and twitter:title from SEO.astro; the dedupe branch is what stops home rendering "The Puzzle School · The Puzzle School".
name: composePageTitle

description: Direction reversals on either axis along a harmonograph trace — a cheap proxy for how intricate the figure is. Feeds the acceptance band that separates a lazy oval from a ball of thread.
name: countTurningPoints

description: The dragon curve: a right-angle fold repeated, walked as an orthogonal lattice that never self-intersects.
name: dragonPoints

description: Escapes interpolated values before they reach the worker's HTML responses.
name: escapeHtml

untestabilityReason.justification: Cloudflare Worker OAuth relay scaffolded by the CMS CLI; runs only on Workers and is unused here (auth.worker is false)

description: Builds the Fibonacci square spiral the way the sequence is built: each side is the sum of the previous two, attached to the growing box on a rotating side. Returns the largest square separately so it can be drawn open.
name: fibonacciTiling

description: Flattens a nav item tree depth-first, each parent immediately before its own children, so resolveContactUrl can scan the whole menu in one pass instead of recursing per match pass. Url-less items are KEPT rather than filtered: a dropdown parent can never itself be the answer, but its children still can, and dropping the parent here would drop the subtree with it. The caller decides what a url-less item means. Exercised through resolveContactUrl's nested-dropdown and url-less-parent cases.
name: flatten

description: Reads the editable navigation singleton per call, for the same reason getSettings does.
name: getNav

untestabilityReason.justification: filesystem read of a JSON singleton; the resolution order it depends on is covered by contentRoot tests

description: Reads the editable site-settings singleton per call rather than at module scope, so a scenario that seeds new settings is visible without restarting the dev server.
name: getSettings

untestabilityReason.justification: filesystem read of a JSON singleton; the resolution order it depends on is covered by contentRoot tests

description: Draws a harmonograph for a seed that passes acceptance, resampling from a derived seed when it does not, and falling back to the closest attempt rather than throwing. Sixty attempts because a raw draw passes about a fifth of the time against four independent checks; this runs inside a page render where a slightly-off figure beats a blank lane.
name: growAcceptableHarmonograph

description: Grows a tree for a seed that passes isAcceptableTree, resampling from a derived seed when it does not. A raw draw only passes about a third of the time, so the budget is 20 rather than a handful. Falls back to the CLOSEST attempt by shortfall rather than throwing, since this runs inside a page render where nobody can catch an exception.
name: growAcceptableTree

description: Builds a Voronoi field for a seed that passes acceptance, resampling from a derived seed when it does not and falling back to the closest attempt rather than throwing, the way growAcceptableTree does.
name: growAcceptableVoronoi

description: Grows the branching structure and returns the geometry plus the two facts acceptance needs that the segment list cannot answer: how many limbs grew, and whether the named bare limb was ever reached. treeSegments is now exactly its segments field, so the older signature and its tests are untouched.
name: growTree

description: Handles the password form POST in the OAuth relay.
name: handlePasswordSubmit

untestabilityReason.justification: Cloudflare Worker OAuth relay scaffolded by the CMS CLI; runs only on Workers and is unused here (auth.worker is false)

description: Renders the OAuth handshake page returned to the popup.
name: handshakePage

untestabilityReason.justification: Cloudflare Worker OAuth relay scaffolded by the CMS CLI; runs only on Workers and is unused here (auth.worker is false)

description: Serialises a harmonograph trace as the single continuous SVG stroke the pen drew.
name: harmonographPath

description: Samples the pen path of a four-pendulum harmonograph: two damped sinusoids summed per axis. The pen lifts at duration times fraction, so what comes back is a stroke stopped mid-swing with its envelope still open rather than a figure settled into a dot.
name: harmonographPoints

description: How far a harmonograph is from acceptable as a single number, zero exactly when it passes every rule. Scores aspect against the lane, busyness, the visible open end, the degenerate collapse to a diagonal line, and the density of the figure's middle. A magnitude rather than a boolean, because the resample loop has to rank failures when no seed qualifies.
name: harmonographShortfall

description: Maps one seed onto one bounded harmonograph option set, drawn in a fixed order so a seed is reproducible. Frequency ratios come from a small set of small-integer intervals including unison, and the second pendulum on each axis is always detuned from the first, because that detune is what makes each pass land rotated from the last.
name: harmonographVariant

description: Frames a harmonograph trace with a margin proportional to the figure, where the tree's is a flat unit. A harmonograph is drawn at amplitudes near 1, so a flat unit would add most of a box width and change the aspect the acceptance band had just checked.
name: harmonographViewBox

description: Turns a page slug into a tree seed with FNV-1a. This is what makes the per-page axis free: about, contact and a page written next year each hash to their own number, so each grows its own tree with no code change. Stable across builds and platforms, because an unstable hash would redraw every committed screenshot on every deploy.
name: hashSeed

description: Wraps an HTML string in a Response with the right content type.
name: htmlResponse

untestabilityReason.justification: Cloudflare Worker OAuth relay scaffolded by the CMS CLI; runs only on Workers and is unused here (auth.worker is false)

description: Whether a harmonograph passes every rule in the envelope, enforced on the geometry that came out rather than on the inputs that went in. Derived from the shortfall score so the two definitions cannot drift.
name: isAcceptableHarmonograph

description: The envelope enforced on the RESULT, not just the inputs. Sampling within bounded ranges is necessary but not sufficient: inside those ranges a seed can still grow every branch stopped early, a crown combed onto one side, or a bare limb the tree never reached. Checks branch count, segment count, aspect, canopy spread and horizontal balance.
name: isAcceptableTree

description: Whether a Voronoi field passes every rule in the envelope, enforced on the geometry that came out rather than the inputs that went in.
name: isAcceptableVoronoi

description: Whether a nav item points at the page being rendered. Compares both sides through normalizeNavPath rather than by string equality, because nav.json stores hand-written urls like '/about' while Astro's default directory build renders the pathname as '/about/' — a strict compare never matches in the built site, which is why no header link was ever inked. Normalizing both sides also covers the mirror case, where a CMS author types the trailing slash and the dev server does not. A NavItem with no url of its own is a dropdown parent and is never current.
name: isCurrentNavPath

description: A stratified scatter of Voronoi sites: one point jittered inside each box of a grid, never leaving its own box. Uniform random points clump, and a clump produces the sliver cell that reads as a drawing mistake rather than as a boundary.
name: jitteredSites

description: The Koch curve: every segment becomes four, turning 60 degrees either way.
name: kochPoints

description: Translates a watcher event under a linked package's real checkout into the symlinked node_modules path the module graph keys under, or null when the file is outside that checkout. The containment check uses a trailing separator so a sibling directory sharing a prefix is not treated as a child.
name: linkedPathForRealFile

description: Vite plugin that makes an edit inside a symlinked @codeyam/cms checkout reach this dev server, defeating the three caches between that file and the browser: it rewrites the immutable node_modules cache header, subscribes the watcher to the real checkout outside the project root, and invalidates the linked module ids that watcher events map to. Only constructed when node_modules/@codeyam/cms is a symlink.
name: liveLinkedCms

description: Expands an axiom by applying production rules a given number of times. Symbols with no rule pass through unchanged, which is what lets the dragon curve carry its bookkeeping symbols.
name: lsystem

description: The share of a harmonograph's sampled points falling in the middle fifth of its bounding box — how much ink piles up at the centre. Damping pulls every pass inward, so a pen left running spirals to a point and lays pass on pass in one small area; the aspect, the turn count and the coverage all still pass while the figure reads as a blot with loops around it. Nothing that reasons about the OUTLINE can see that, so the middle is measured on its own.
name: measureCoreDensity

description: How many cells of a coarse grid over its own bounding box a harmonograph's stroke visits, as a fraction. This is the degeneracy test: a collapsed draw is a diagonal LINE, which fills its bounding box corner to corner and passes every aspect check while looking nothing like a harmonograph. Only occupancy tells a line from a rosette — a straight draw measures about 0.04 against a healthy 0.4 or more.
name: measureCoverage

description: Encodes words as morse laid out left to right at classic proportions — dash three units, symbol gap one, letter gap three, word gap seven. Unencodable characters are skipped rather than guessed at.
name: morseLine

description: Reduces a path to a canonical form for comparison: query string and hash dropped, one trailing slash stripped, whitespace trimmed, lowercased. The site root is deliberately preserved as '/' rather than collapsing to the empty string, which would otherwise let a Home nav item match every page on the site.
name: normalizeNavPath

description: Draws the three sides of an open square — down the left, across, back up — so the spiral's largest frame never closes.
name: openRectPath

description: Distance outside an inclusive range, or zero within it. The primitive every proportion rule in treeShortfall is expressed in, so each rule contributes a comparable magnitude rather than a bare pass or fail — which is what lets the resample loop rank near-misses instead of picking arbitrarily.
name: outOfBand

description: Renders the password prompt page for a locked preview.
name: passwordFormPage

untestabilityReason.justification: Cloudflare Worker OAuth relay scaffolded by the CMS CLI; runs only on Workers and is unused here (auth.worker is false)

description: The bounding box of a set of points, shared by every structure that frames itself to its own extent. A zero extent collapses to 1 rather than 0 deliberately: callers divide by these to normalise, and a figure drawn perfectly flat on one axis is the degenerate case acceptance exists to reject, so it must arrive as a bad score rather than a NaN.
name: pointBounds

description: Area of a simple polygon by the shoelace formula. Exported because it is how the partition's defining property is checked, that the cells tile the frame exactly; counting cells instead would pass a slivered field just as happily as a good one.
name: polygonArea

description: Chooses an internal page's prose shape from its body: two or more sections keep the two-column layout with the branching structure in the gap, one or none get the centred single column flanked by a harmonograph and a Voronoi field. Derived from the body rather than declared in frontmatter, so a page written from the CMS gets the right layout by writing, with no field to remember and no code change.
name: proseLayoutFor

description: A fresh seed for the per-visit regrow, deliberately in the same unsigned 32-bit space hashSeed produces. If the two ranges drifted apart, trees grown in the browser would quietly become a different population from the trees grown at build time from a page slug.
name: randomTreeSeed

description: Reads and parses one editable JSON singleton from the resolved data root.
name: readSingleton

untestabilityReason.justification: a filesystem read; the root-resolution logic it depends on is covered by the contentRoot tests

description: Resolves where the site footer's Contact link should point by reading the CMS-editable nav singleton, so moving or renaming the Contact page in the menu retargets the footer with it. Walks the nav depth-first and matches in two passes: first any item whose label contains 'contact' case-insensitively, then any item whose url starts with /contact. Items without a url — dropdown parents that only group children — are skipped so the footer never emits href=undefined. Falls back to /contact when nothing matches, which is always a live route because the page is not nav-gated. Pure by design: it takes the already-loaded nav rather than reading src/data itself, unlike site.ts which resolves the data root with fs at module scope.
name: resolveContactUrl

description: The absolute content root the collections read from — the codeyam sandbox during a session, committed src/content in production.
name: resolveContentRoot

description: The absolute data root the settings and nav singletons read from, resolved the same way as the content root.
name: resolveDataRoot

description: Resolves a content or data root in precedence order: env override, then the .codeyam/tmp sidecar, then the committed default.
name: resolveRoot

description: Decides which seed a tree grows from. The precedence is the point: an explicit seed wins so the variations sheet can pin specific trees, otherwise the key is hashed, and a caller naming nothing falls back to one shared default tree rather than a random one, because an unseeded component should be stable across builds.
name: resolveTreeSeed

description: Trims float noise to two decimals so generated path data stays readable in devtools.
name: round

description: Counts the depth-3 headings in a rendered body. Counting that specific depth rather than any heading is load-bearing: the page title is rendered by the header, and a sub-heading inside one section must not promote the page to two.
name: sectionCount

description: A deterministic mulberry32 generator. The site is static, so unseeded randomness would redraw every structure on every build and churn every committed screenshot; the same seed gives the same figure forever.
name: seededRandom

description: Samples one sine wave across a width at a fixed phase, so waves of differing amplitude and period share an origin. `fraction` stops the wave short of the frame — the incompleteness dial.
name: sinePath

description: Builds one Voronoi field: places the sites, sets one or two aside unresolved, partitions what is left, and opens one cell. The unresolved sites are removed BEFORE the partition rather than hidden after it, so the surrounding cells are computed as though those points were never there and genuinely overrun where a boundary should be.
name: tessellate

description: Joins a list of points into an SVG polyline `d` attribute, rounding coordinates to two decimals so generated paths stay readable.
name: toPath

description: Samples a harmonograph and measures the four things acceptance asks about it that the point list cannot answer at a glance: turning points, how much of its own bounding box the stroke visits, how far apart its two ends are, and how much ink piles up in the middle.
name: traceHarmonograph

description: Builds the SVG transform string for one puzzle piece: a rotation about the mark's centre, plus an inset and scale for the four diagonal pieces.
name: transformFor

untestabilityReason.justification: formats a transform string from two arguments; the geometry it produces is covered by the Mark component scenarios

description: The bounding box of a grown tree — origin plus width and height, with a floor of one unit so a degenerate figure cannot produce a zero-sized box and divide by zero downstream. Shared by treeViewBox and the acceptance checks so the frame and the proportion rules are measured off exactly the same geometry.
name: treeBounds

description: The grown geometry alone, for every caller that only ever wanted the lines. Now exactly growTree(options).segments — kept as its own export so the signature the component and the five existing tree tests depend on did not have to move when growTree started returning branch counts alongside the segments.
name: treeSegments

description: How far a grown tree is from acceptable, as a single number — zero exactly when it passes every rule. A boolean is what callers want but is not enough to CHOOSE with: when no seed in the resample budget produces an acceptable tree, something still has to be drawn, and ranking the failures needs a magnitude. isAcceptableTree is derived from this, so the predicate and the ranking cannot drift apart.
name: treeShortfall

description: Maps an arbitrary seed onto one bounded parameter set drawn from TREE_ENVELOPE. Free-form randomisation of TreeOptions would eventually produce a bald stick or a shrub; sampling from declared ranges is what makes within some constraints a testable object rather than a hope.
name: treeVariant

description: The viewBox framing a grown tree, with a one-unit margin so the outermost stroke is not clipped. Extracted because BOTH the server render and the browser regrow need it; left inline in the component the two renders could silently drift into framing the same tree differently.
name: treeViewBox

description: Walks an L-system string as turtle graphics and returns the points visited. `fraction` walks only part of the forward moves, which is what makes a fragment a fragment.
name: turtle

description: A small cross marking a site the partition has no cell for yet, the way an unplotted point gets noted.
name: unresolvedMarkPath

description: Partitions a frame by nearest neighbour, each cell being the frame cut back by the perpendicular bisector against every other site. Built by half-plane clipping rather than triangulation, which keeps the module free of a Delaunay dependency; the clip rectangle is larger than the visible lane, so cells run off its edges unresolved instead of being tidied into a box.
name: voronoiCells

description: Every stroke of a Voronoi field in draw order, cells first then the unresolved marks. Shared by the server render and the per-visit redraw so the two cannot drift into drawing the same field differently.
name: voronoiPaths

description: How far a Voronoi field is from acceptable as a single number, zero exactly when it passes. Scores cell count against a band, rejects slivers by area against the mean, and penalises a field that lost either deliberate incompleteness, since a feature that silently failed to apply is invisible in a geometry list.
name: voronoiShortfall

description: Maps one seed onto one bounded Voronoi option set. The grid is deliberately tall and narrow, because the lane is 123 by 365 and cells that are roughly square need about three times as many rows as columns to fill it without stretching.
name: voronoiVariant

description: Frames a Voronoi field at the lane it was generated for, so preserveAspectRatio has no distortion to apply and the cells run off the lane's own edges.
name: voronoiViewBox
